# PocketOne

> PocketOne is a community fork of PocketBase (one Go binary: database, auth, files, realtime, admin UI) with extensions for point-in-time recovery, backups, mail, many instances on one server, deploys, tokens and OAuth, MCP, and PocketPages server-rendered sites.

PocketOne takes the same commands and flags as PocketBase, plus its own; core PocketBase topics live at https://pocketbase.io/docs. Agent Skills for PocketOne and PocketPages: https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/agent (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone`).

Every page below in one file: https://pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt

## Get started

- [What is PocketOne?](https://pocketone.dev/docs/overview): PocketOne is a community fork of PocketBase. Its core changes are kept small; everything else is an extension.
- [Installation](https://pocketone.dev/docs/installation): Install PocketOne with Homebrew, a release download or go build, and keep it up to date.
- [Coming from PocketBase](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketbase): PocketOne is PocketBase with more built in. What stays the same, what's added, and where to read about the parts that come straight from PocketBase.
- [Teach your coding agent](https://pocketone.dev/docs/agents): Teach Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding agents PocketOne and PocketPages with our Agent Skills and llms.txt.

## New in PocketOne

- [Everything new](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features): Everything PocketOne adds to PocketBase, side by side with what PocketBase gives you. All built in and on by default.
- [Point-in-time restore](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/restore): Put your app's data back as it was at any moment in the last few days, from the dashboard, your terminal or an agent.
- [Deploy and live sync](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/deploy): Send your app's hooks, migrations, pages and public files to a running PocketOne app with one command, and keep a folder in step while you work.
- [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote): Manage any PocketOne app from your terminal, a script or an agent. Every extension API is a command, a REST endpoint and an MCP tool at once.
- [API tokens and OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/tokens): Give a script, a CI job or a service its own long-lived token, limited to what it needs, and revoke it whenever you like. Apps and tools can also sign in to get one.
- [MCP for AI agents](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/mcp): Connect Claude or another MCP client to your app, sign in once, and let it work with your data and settings with exactly your rights.
- [Bulk mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/bulk-mail): Send a newsletter or announcement to your app's own users, from the dashboard, your terminal or an agent.
- [PocketPages sites](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/sites): Serve server-rendered pages from a pb_pages folder next to your data, with PocketPages, built into every PocketOne app.
- [QuickJS hooks](https://pocketone.dev/docs/quickjs): PocketOne runs pb_hooks on QuickJS, a drop-in replacement for PocketBase's JS engine that adds imports, TypeScript, async handlers, shared globals and hard memory and time limits.
- [pocketone.yaml](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketone-yaml): Put your app's settings in one file instead of a line of flags, keep secrets in a .env beside it, and set any extension's options.

## Extend PocketOne

- [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/how-pocketone-fits-together): How PocketOne extensions work together: every extension API is a named, versioned contract that any extension can provide.
- [Writing an extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension): How to write a PocketOne extension.
- [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts): Every contract in PocketOne: what it promises and which extensions provide, require and work with it.
- [Extensions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions): Every extension in PocketOne, grouped by what it's for.

## Reference

- [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli): Every command of the pocketone binary: PocketBase's own, the standard extensions', and one per contract operation.
- [REST](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/rest): Every contract API of a PocketOne app with its standard extensions: method, path, token scope and input.
- [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp): Every MCP tool a PocketOne app's contracts add at /mcp, with its token scope and arguments.
- [pocketone.yaml](https://pocketone.dev/docs/config-reference): Every section of the pocketone.yaml config file, generated from the pocketone binary.

## Contracts: By name

- [bulkmail/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1): Run bulk mail campaigns: count an audience; start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign.
- [cache.clear/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1): Emptying an app's cache buckets, one or all, from the dashboard, the CLI or an agent.
- [cache/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache/v1): Named buckets of bytes an app keeps for a while, with limits and eviction; memory, disk or a shared cache behind it.
- [cli.commands/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cli.commands/v1): The pocketone command tree: every contract operation as a remote command by default; extensions replace or add commands.
- [deploy/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/deploy/v1): A project's code files on an app: check, upload, commit, list, read, write, delete, tree.
- [gate/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/gate/v1): What admits requests on a multisite host: peer checks, client IPs and rate limits, in order.
- [http.wrap/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/http.wrap/v1): Middleware around everything a multisite host serves, nested in order.
- [instance.source/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.source/v1): The instance record a multisite host serves, and where the records come from.
- [mail.fallback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.fallback/v1): Where an app's mail goes when SMTP is off: a chain of providers that send it or pass it on.
- [mail.feedback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1): Mail providers' reports (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) received at one place and raised as events any extension can act on.
- [mail.suppression/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1): Addresses an app must not send bulk mail to, and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries.
- [mcp/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mcp/v1): The app's MCP endpoint at /mcp, with every provided contract's operations as tools.
- [oauth/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/oauth/v1): The app's OAuth 2.1 authorization server, so the CLI and MCP clients can sign in.
- [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1): Remote control of an app: whoami, status, restart, logs. The base every client starts from.
- [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1): Put an app's data back as it was at a moment: from continuous history, or the latest backup before it.
- [runtime/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1): What runs a multisite host's instances (as isolates, in containers), in preference order.
- [settings/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1): The settings an app's admins change for its extensions, one API for all of them.
- [templates/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/templates/v1): An extension's own pages as Go templates a project can eject and edit.
- [tls/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tls/v1): The TLS of a multisite host's listener: automatic certificates instead of certificate files.
- [tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tokens/v1): An app's API tokens: check one, register scopes, read a request's token, limit in-process requests; the token API.
- [vacuum/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/vacuum/v1): Compacting an app's databases so freed space goes back to the disk, and when it last happened.

## Extensions: Standard extensions

- [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls): Certificates on demand and wildcards through ACME.
- [Backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups): Restore an app to a moment from its own backups: the latest one before it. On by default.
- [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail): Campaigns to your app's own users, with audiences from a collection, a view or SQL.
- [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache): Cache buckets for every app in the process from one shared store: bytes or Go values, a budget per bucket, LRU/MRU/FIFO/LIFO eviction, TTLs, a cold disk tier that keeps identical values once.
- [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config): The pocketone.yaml config file, with secrets in a .env beside it.
- [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy): pocketone deploy, dev, pull and logs, and the deploy API.
- [JSVM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm): PocketOne's JS engine: one QuickJS VM per app, real globals, async handlers, hard limits.
- [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp): An MCP endpoint at /mcp so agents can manage your app and call its tools.
- [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/extension): Server-rendered pages from a pb_pages folder (formerly PocketPages).
- [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr): Point-in-time restore of your database with Litestream. On by default.
- [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes): Named remotes and saved logins for the pocketone command.
- [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect): File downloads as short-lived signed S3 redirects.
- [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings): One API for the settings an app's admins change for its extensions. On by default.
- [Templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates): Theme an extension's own pages (the OAuth sign-in screens): eject its templates to pb_templates and edit them.
- [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens): Long-lived API tokens with scopes.
- [Tokens: OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth): Tokens: OAuth
- [Upgrade](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/upgrade): pocketone upgrade to the latest release, keeping the old executable.
- [Vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum): Compact your app's SQLite databases on a schedule, so space freed by deleted records goes back to the disk.

## Extensions: Run many instances

- [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker): A host provider that runs each instance in its own container.
- [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge): Forwards each request to the edge that owns the instance.
- [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall): Peer allow-lists, trusted proxies and rate limits for a host.
- [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership): A control plane and its edges, across regions.
- [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite): Many instances behind one listener, routed by hostname, run by one provider.
- [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker): Hundreds of PocketBase instances in one Go process, routed by hostname.
- [Pocker: Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker/pocker): Pocker: Pocker
- [Sandbox](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox): Confines untrusted JS hooks, SQL and outbound network.
- [Schedules](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/schedules): Planned. Scheduled webhooks that wake sleeping instances.
- [Stats](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/stats): Measures disk use and last request for each instance a host serves.

## Extensions: Services for your instances

- [Mail Relay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay): Outgoing mail for instances without SMTP, through your relay, with limits.
- [S3 Fallback](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback): A default bucket for uploads and backups when an instance has no S3 of its own.
- [Server Timing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/servertiming): Server-Timing headers for each step of a request.
- [WASM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm): Bring your own WASM: Go, Rust or Zig modules called from pb_hooks, each a closed box.

## Extensions: Sell it as a service

- [Lemon Squeezy Adapter](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenant-billing-ls): Planned. Lemon Squeezy as the billing provider.
- [Multitenant](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants): Planned. Accounts that own instances: quotas, owner logins, tokens and an API.
- [Multitenant Billing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenant-billing): Planned. Plans, quotas and the billing provider hook for Multitenant.

## Extensions: For extension authors

- [Bundle](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bundle): An app's hooks, migrations and public files embedded in the binary.
- [Contracts](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/README.md)
- [Dev Users](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go)
- [Extension Kit](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/extkit/extkit.go)
- [Mail Trap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap): Dev mode: mail from an app without SMTP lands in a built-in inbox.
- [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard): The extensions every PocketOne app has, as one set a host configures.

## Pages

- [Home](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages): No-build, server-rendered multi-page apps for PocketOne. PocketPages is built into the pocketone binary as the pages extension.
- [PocketPages v1 specification](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/spec): Pages: PocketPages v1 specification

## Pages: Introduction

- [Overview of PocketPages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/overview): PocketPages is server-rendered multi-page apps for PocketOne, from a pb_pages folder of EJS and Markdown files.
- [Moving from PocketPages 0.x](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/moving-from-0x): What changed between the PocketPages npm package (0.x) and PocketPages v1 in PocketOne.
- [Coding agents](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/agents): Teach Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding agents PocketPages v1 with the pocketpages Agent Skill and llms.txt.

## Pages: Getting Started

- [Installation](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/installation): Run PocketPages v1 on PocketOne with the pages extension, using a pb_pages folder.
- [Starter Kits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/starter-kits): Start a new PocketPages app from a starter kit with pocketone pages create.

## Pages: Basics

- [Creating a Page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/creating-a-page): Create .ejs and .md files in pb_pages to add pages, with index files and nested folders mapping to URLs.
- [Directory Structure](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/directory-structure): How a pb_pages folder is organized, and the special +, _, - and . prefixes.
- [Routing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/routing): How files in pb_pages map to URLs: pages, [param] segments, groups, API routes, static files, and which route wins.
- [Accessing Parameters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/parameters): Read route parameters from [param] file and folder names with ctx.params, and query strings with ctx.req.query().
- [Loading Data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data): Load data inline in templates or in a +page.js file with load and per-method handlers.
- [API Routes and JSON](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes): Serve JSON and other non-HTML responses from +api.js files and ctx.res.json.

## Pages: Templating

- [EJS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ejs): The EJS tags PocketPages supports, escaping rules, and what's in scope inside a template.
- [Markdown](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown): .md pages and partials run through EJS, then Markdown, with YAML front matter passed to meta().
- [JSX and TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx): Write pages, layouts, partials and error pages as .jsx or .tsx components, rendered to HTML on the server with no build step.
- [Partials](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials): Include reusable templates from _private folders with include(name, locals).
- [Layouts and Slots](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/layouts): Wrap pages with +layout.ejs files, and pass content between pages and layouts with named slots.

## Pages: Security and Content

- [Private files](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/private-files): How _private folders hold partials and JS modules for include() and ctx.resolve(), and which names are never routed.
- [Middleware](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware): +middleware.js files run root first for every route below them, with one (ctx, next) signature.
- [Asset Management](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/asset-management): Static files in pb_pages get content-hashed URLs through asset() for long-term caching.
- [Static content](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content): Files in pb_pages that aren't pages or framework files are served as-is, with content types and ETags.
- [Managing Secrets](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets): Read API keys and other secrets from environment variables with ctx.env().

## Pages: Configuration

- [+config.js](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/config): Turn on built-in plugins, add JS plugins, and enable debug output from pb_pages/+config.js.
- [Caching](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/caching): How PocketPages caches templates, static files and fingerprinted assets.
- [Errors](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors): How PocketPages turns thrown errors into responses, ctx.httpError(), and custom +error and +404 pages.
- [Debugging](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/debugging): Dev mode, debug in +config.js, and logging with ctx.log.
- [Going Live](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/deploying): Deploy a PocketPages app by putting pb_pages next to pb_data on a PocketOne server (pages is built in).

## Pages: Plugins

- [Overview](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins): Built-in plugins (auth, realtime) and JS plugins such as the Datastar add-on, turned on in +config.js.
- [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth): The built-in auth plugin keeps PocketBase auth in a cookie and adds ctx.session sign-in methods.
- [Datastar](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar): The Datastar add-on adds ctx.datastar helpers for Datastar script tags, SSE patches and signals.
- [Realtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime): The built-in realtime plugin sends messages to PocketBase realtime subscribers with ctx.realtime.send().
- [Authoring](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring): Write a JS plugin for PocketPages v1, a factory that returns onRequest, extendContext and transform hooks.

## Pages: ctx Reference

- [Overview](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx): Reference for ctx, the one object per request passed to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.
- [req](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/req): The request - method, URL, query parameters, headers, cookies, body, uploaded files and client IP.
- [res](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res): The response - status, headers, cookies, redirects with flash messages, JSON, HTML, text, files and server-sent events.
- [data, params, route](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data): The shared data object, route parameters and the matched route.
- [flash](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash): One-time messages carried across a redirect in a cookie.
- [auth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/auth): The authenticated record for the request, or null.
- [app](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/app): The app - records, collections and settings.
- [pb (JS SDK)](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/pb): Query your app with the PocketBase JS SDK from page code, as the signed-in user.
- [env](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/env): Read environment variables.
- [log](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/log): Write to the app's log with debug, info, warn and error.
- [meta](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/meta): A per-request key/value store for page metadata such as title and description.
- [asset](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset): Content-hashed URLs for static files in pb_pages.
- [resolve](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve): Load a module or file from a _private folder.
- [store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/store): The app's in-memory store, shared across requests.

## Pages: Going Further

- [JavaScript Runtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm): Where page code runs, what it can reach, and using npm packages from pb_pages/node_modules.

## Pages: Guides

- [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication): Sign users in and out with the auth plugin - passwords, one-time passwords, OAuth2 and anonymous sessions.
- [HTMX Integration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/htmx): Use HTMX with PocketPages: route organization, HTML fragments without layouts, shared partials, forms, and realtime updates.
- [Realtime Events](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/realtime): Send realtime messages from pages with the realtime plugin, and receive them in the browser with the PocketBase JS SDK.
- [Custom Domains on Fly+Cloudflare](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/custom-domain-fly-cloudflare): Step-by-step process to configure DNS records, SSL certificates, and domain verification between Fly.io and Cloudflare. Includes specific settings for A/AAAA records, CNAME verification, and SSL/TLS encryption modes.
- [Google OAuth2](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2): Set up Google OAuth2 sign-in for a PocketPages app with the auth plugin.
- [Outgoing Email with Amazon SES](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses): Step-by-step configuration of AWS Simple Email Service (SES) with Google Suite, including DNS records, DKIM setup, SMTP credentials, and PocketBase integration for production email delivery.
- [Setting up a new email domain in Google Suite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail): Complete walkthrough for configuring email domains in Google Suite, including domain verification, Gmail activation, catch-all email setup, MX record configuration, and sender account integration.

## Optional

- [PocketBase compatibility](https://pocketone.dev/docs/compatibility): Live results of PocketBase's own test suite, unmodified, run against PocketOne's core on every core change and daily.
